description: Experience the delicate flavors of Cantonese cuisine with this classic Steamed Whole Fish. This elegant dish highlights the natural sweetness of fresh fish, complemented by aromatic ginger, scallions, and a savory soy sauce dressing. It is a symbol of prosperity and a beloved centerpiece for family meals and celebrations.

ingredients.item: Whole Fish (e.g., Branzino, Red Snapper, Tilapia)

ingredients.notes: about 3 inches, half sliced, half julienned
half cut into 2-inch sections, half julienned for garnish

instructions.title: Prepare the Fish
instructions.text: Ensure your whole fish is thoroughly cleaned, scaled, and gutted. Pat the fish completely dry with paper towels. Make two to three shallow diagonal cuts on both sides of the fish. This helps the fish cook evenly and absorb flavors. Lightly season the fish inside and out with a pinch of white pepper.

instructions.title: Flavor the Fish
instructions.text: Place half of the sliced ginger and 2-3 sections of scallion inside the fish cavity. Arrange the remaining sliced ginger and scallion sections on top of and under the fish. If using, drizzle a teaspoon of Shaoxing wine over the fish. This infuses the fish with aromatic flavors during steaming.

instructions.title: Prepare the Steamer
instructions.text: Fill a wok or large pot with water, ensuring it does not touch the steaming rack. Bring the water to a rolling boil over high heat. Place a heatproof plate or steaming dish with the prepared fish onto the steaming rack. Ensure there is enough space around the fish for steam to circulate.

instructions.title: Steam the Fish
instructions.text: Cover the wok or pot tightly with a lid. Steam the fish for 8-12 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fish. A good indicator of doneness is when the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Do not overcook, as this will dry out the fish.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce and Garnish
instructions.text: While the fish is steaming, combine the light soy sauce and sesame oil in a small bowl to create the dressing. Once the fish is cooked, carefully remove it from the steamer. Discard the cooked ginger and scallions from the plate, as they may contain fishy odors. Garnish the steamed fish with the fresh julienned ginger and julienned scallions.

instructions.title: Sizzle and Serve
instructions.text: Heat the neutral cooking oil in a small saucepan over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Carefully pour the hot oil evenly over the julienned ginger and scallions on the fish. This sizzles the aromatics, releasing their full fragrance. Finally, pour the prepared soy sauce dressing over the fish. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately with steamed rice.

tips: Choose the freshest fish available. Look for clear eyes, red gills, and firm flesh. Freshness is paramount for steamed fish.
Do not oversteam the fish. The ideal texture is tender and flaky, not dry. A 1.5-2 lb fish typically needs 8-12 minutes.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can add a few slices of fresh shiitake mushrooms or a sprinkle of white pepper inside the fish cavity before steaming.
